name: TonePush 0.11.0
body:
TonePush 0.11.0 gets more pedals connected and importing. A StompStation PRO that sends text TonePush cannot read now opens instead of failing to connect, `.hlx` import works on an HX Effects, and a new `batch` command runs a whole preset build over one connection, in seconds rather than minutes. Windows now ships as a signed `.msi` only.

**Download TonePush:** [Mac](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.11.0/tonepush-v0.11.0-macos-universal.dmg) · [Windows](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.11.0/tonepush-v0.11.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.msi) · [Windows ARM](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.11.0/tonepush-v0.11.0-aarch64-pc-windows-msvc.msi) · [Linux](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.11.0/tonepush-v0.11.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz) · [Linux ARM](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.11.0/tonepush-v0.11.0-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz) · [Linux AppImage](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.11.0/tonepush-0.11.0-x86_64.AppImage)

## New

- **`tonepush batch` runs many commands over one connection.** Give it a file of commands, or pipe them in. The whole file is read first, so a typo stops it before the pedal is touched; a line that fails is reported and the rest still run; `sleep <ms>` gives the pedal time where it needs it. In @AC6y86's measurements on an HX Effects, a 100-command preset build went from about 12 minutes to about 11 seconds. See [the CLI guide](https://docs.tonepush.rocks/using-the-cli/). By @crmne, from the design and measurements of @AC6y86 (#8).
- **Windows releases are signed**, and Windows ships as the `.msi` only. By @crmne in #45 and #70.

## Fixed

- **A StompStation PRO opens when it sends a byte that is not valid text.** It used to stop at "VoidX frame was not UTF-8". The character shows as `�` and the pedal connects. By @crmne; thanks @christoph-krionx (#74).
- **`.hlx` import works on an HX Effects.** Every menu in a file was sent as a number the pedal refused, so all imports failed with error -3. By @crmne; thanks @robbuckles, who found the cause and tested it on a pedal (#44).
- **A failed preset write says what differed**, so a pedal that reports a failure can show which field it kept for itself. By @crmne; thanks @robbuckles (#44).
- **`install.sh` replaces a udev rule from before StompStation PRO support**, which left the pedal's serial port closed to the editor. By @crmne.
- **An HX Effects backup no longer times out** reading the pedal's settings. Fixed by #31 in 0.10.0 and now confirmed on an HX Effects by @robbuckles (#9).

## Known limitations

- The Windows setup program (`-setup.exe`) is gone. Installs from 0.9.1 on move to the `.msi` through their own update, keeping their folder, desktop shortcut and settings. **A copy still on 0.9.0 must run the `.msi` once by hand.**
- The StompStation PRO fix was tested in unit tests and on firmware 2.2.6, not on 2.2.7, where it was reported. Writes are allowed across 2.2.x, but TonePush has been verified on 2.2.6 only.
- Restoring a preset on an HX Effects can report a failure although it landed (#44).
- An HX Stomp on firmware 3.80 that disconnects after a few seconds (#5), and a StompStation PRO the editor cannot open while the command line finds it (#34), are still being investigated. The error on the connect page tells us what to fix.
- `batch` and the import fix have not been run on hardware by the maintainer; the import fix was tested on an HX Effects by its reporter.
- Helix LT and Helix Rack have not been tested on real hardware.

## Thanks

@robbuckles for finding the import bug and proving the fix on a pedal, @AC6y86 for the `batch` design, and @christoph-krionx, @Bei894, @fruzz-urban and @gencinoza for reporting problems and testing on their own pedals.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/compare/v0.10.0...v0.11.0

name: TonePush 0.10.0
body:
TonePush 0.10.0 brings the Helix Floor: its presets open, its eight setlists back up and show in a picker above the presets, controllers carry the Floor's own names, snapshots show their colours, and models that would not fit on a path are greyed out before the pedal refuses them. Moving or inserting a block now keeps everything that points at it. Crash reports can be turned on, and are off until you do.

**Download TonePush:** [Mac](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.10.0/tonepush-v0.10.0-macos-universal.dmg) · [Windows](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.10.0/tonepush-v0.10.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.msi) · [Windows ARM](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.10.0/tonepush-v0.10.0-aarch64-pc-windows-msvc.msi) · [Linux](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.10.0/tonepush-v0.10.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz) · [Linux ARM](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.10.0/tonepush-v0.10.0-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz) · [Linux AppImage](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.10.0/tonepush-0.10.0-x86_64.AppImage)

![TonePush on a Helix Floor: the Rehearsal setlist chosen above presets 01A to 05D, Plexi Crunch loaded with its chain and Path 1 at 87% DSP used, the amp's knobs below and the library at the bottom](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.10.0/tonepush-v0.10.0-helix-floor.png)

![The light theme on a Helix Floor with the Snapshots view open: eight snapshots, each with its colour beside its number, which blocks each one turns on, and the values each one sets](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.10.0/tonepush-v0.10.0-snapshots-light.png)

## New

- **The Helix Floor works.** Its presets open, including ones with a cleared snapshot name or the Floor's own controller assignments, they are labelled in banks of four (01A to 32D), and a whole-pedal backup reads all eight setlists. Reading, backing up, editing and saving were tested on a Floor at firmware 3.80. By @Jazzpirate in #29, #30, #31 and #32.
- **Choose which setlist the preset list shows.** On a pedal with more than one, a picker sits above the presets. Showing another setlist loads nothing; picking a preset there loads it. By @Jazzpirate in #33.
- **Controllers carry each pedal's own names.** On a Floor, the assignment menu and the Footswitches view offer FS1 to FS11, EXP 1 to 3, the Variax knobs, MIDI CC and Snapshots, and the footswitch board wraps onto more rows instead of squeezing them into one. By @Jazzpirate in #37.
- **Snapshot colours on a Helix Floor.** Each snapshot's colour shows beside its name, and the current snapshot's heading has a menu to change its colour, rename it or copy it over another. By @Jazzpirate in #43.
- **Models that would not fit are greyed out on a Helix Floor.** The model browser shows each model's share of the path's DSP and greys out the ones the pedal would refuse, and the board says how much of each path is in use. By @Jazzpirate in #42.
- **Eight snapshots fit** in the Snapshots view and along the top, where their names used to run over the preset's name. By @Jazzpirate in #35.
- **Crash reports, only if you turn them on.** TonePush asks once, and Settings has a switch. A report says where the editor crashed, on which version and system, and never your name, files, tones or presets. By @crmne.

## Fixed

- **Moving a block keeps its controllers, footswitches and snapshot states.** They used to stay on the slot it left, and on a Helix Floor the saved preset could stop opening. By @Jazzpirate in #40.
- **A block added in a gap lands between the blocks either side of it**, and inserting no longer says a row is full while it has room. It never moves a block across a split or join. By @Jazzpirate and @crmne in #39.
- **An HX Effects keeps sending what happens on the pedal.** It used to fall silent after about 35 seconds until it was power cycled. By @anthonybartczak in #25.
- **A StompStation PRO that is found but cannot be opened says why** on the connect page, instead of "Not found". By @crmne; thanks @Bei894 (#34).
- **Restoring a stored preset on a Helix Floor no longer reports a failure** when the preset landed. By @crmne; thanks @Jazzpirate (#36).
- **A cab's Mic under a controller shows as Mic**, not as the cab's Distance. By @Jazzpirate in #38.

## Known limitations

- Helix LT and Helix Rack have not been tested on real hardware.
- After a TonePush session ends, a Helix Floor's display can freeze until it is power cycled, though it still responds to its switches (#28).
- A Mic assignment can be read, but not changed from TonePush yet.
- An HX Effects backup may still time out while reading the pedal's settings (#9). The Helix Floor fix for the same symptom should cover it, but nobody has tried it on an HX Effects yet.
- An HX Effects refuses `.hlx` imports with error -3 (#44), and an HX Stomp on firmware 3.80 that disconnects after a few seconds (#5) is still being investigated.
- This release still includes the Windows setup programs (`-setup.exe`), so that copies of 0.9.0 can update.

## Thanks

@Jazzpirate for bringing up the Helix Floor and testing every change on one, @anthonybartczak for the HX Effects fix, and @Bei894, @robbuckles, @fruzz-urban and @gencinoza for reporting problems and testing on their own pedals.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/compare/v0.9.1...v0.10.0

name: TonePush 0.9.1
body:
TonePush 0.9.1 moves the Windows installer to a Windows Installer package (`.msi`), because antivirus engines flag the old setup program. If you installed TonePush with the 0.9.0 setup program, **Update** brings you 0.9.1 through that setup program as before, and the update after it moves you onto the new installer by itself, in the same folder and with your settings.

**Download TonePush:** [Mac](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.9.1/tonepush-v0.9.1-macos-universal.dmg) · [Windows](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.9.1/tonepush-v0.9.1-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.msi) · [Windows ARM](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.9.1/tonepush-v0.9.1-aarch64-pc-windows-msvc.msi) · [Linux](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.9.1/tonepush-v0.9.1-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz) · [Linux ARM](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.9.1/tonepush-v0.9.1-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz) · [Linux AppImage](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.9.1/tonepush-0.9.1-x86_64.AppImage)

## New

- **A Windows Installer package for x64 and ARM.** Like the setup program, it installs for you alone without administrator rights, adds TonePush to the Start menu and installs the `tonepush` command-line tool. Installed over a copy from the 0.9.0 setup program, it takes that copy's place: same folder, its desktop shortcut kept, one entry in Settings, Apps. From 0.9.1 on, updates from inside TonePush use it. By @crmne.

## Fixed

- **Uninstalling while TonePush runs no longer leaves half of it behind.** The new installer, and the uninstaller of this release's setup program, wait until TonePush and any `tonepush` command have quit. By @crmne.
- **TonePush uses less memory for the fonts it falls back on** for scripts Inter does not cover. By @crmne.

## Known limitations

- This release still includes the setup programs (`-setup.exe`), so that copies of 0.9.0 can update; later releases ship the `.msi` only. A copy unpacked from the Windows zip keeps updating as a zip.
- The installer never closes TonePush for you; it asks you to quit it first.
- An HX Effects backup can still time out while reading the pedal's settings (#9), and an HX Stomp on firmware 3.80 that stays on "transferring data" (#5) is still being investigated.

## Thanks

Everyone who reported problems and tested on their own pedals.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/compare/v0.9.0...v0.9.1

name: TonePush 0.9.0
body:
TonePush 0.9.0 puts your library under the editor: click a tone to hear it on the pedal without writing anything, then keep it or put the preset back. Tones, presets, setlists and files drag to where they go, and you can publish to TonePush for everyone or only for yourself. The StompStation PRO saves on firmware 2.2, its 2.x chain is drawn and edited with parallel paths and free positions, and Windows finds it. Windows also gets an installer.

**Download TonePush:** [Mac](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.9.0/tonepush-v0.9.0-macos-universal.dmg) · [Windows](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.9.0/tonepush-v0.9.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc-setup.exe) · [Windows ARM](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.9.0/tonepush-v0.9.0-aarch64-pc-windows-msvc-setup.exe) · [Linux](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.9.0/tonepush-v0.9.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz) · [Linux ARM](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.9.0/tonepush-v0.9.0-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz) · [Linux AppImage](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.9.0/tonepush-0.9.0-x86_64.AppImage)

![TonePush on an HX Stomp playing Dream Pop from the library in 01B: the chain and knobs above, a bar saying Plexi Crunch waits with its unsaved changes, with Put Plexi Crunch back and Keep in 01B, and the library's tones below](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.9.0/tonepush-v0.9.0-audition.png)

![The light theme on a StompStation PRO at firmware 2.0.10: its chain of fourteen positions with the delay and reverb in parallel, locks on the fixed blocks and free positions between them, the delay's knobs below and the library at the bottom](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.9.0/tonepush-v0.9.0-pro-router-light.png)

## New

- **The library sits under the editor.** Tones, Setlists and Cloud share a pane along the bottom that you can resize or fold (Ctrl L), so the preset stays in view. The pedal's backups, impulse responses, NAM models and settings open from its card in the sidebar. By @crmne.
- **Click a tone to hear it.** It plays in the loaded preset without writing the pedal's memory, and the preset waits with its unsaved changes. **Keep in 01B** (Enter) keeps the tone, **Put back** (Esc) brings the preset back, and the arrow keys step through the tones. Knobs you turn while trying a tone stay with the tone. TonePush's tones, a setlist's slots and older versions play the same way. By @crmne.
- **Drag things to where they go.** Tones onto a preset, the board, a setlist's slot or the Cloud tab; presets onto the Tones tab; setlists onto the presets; tone files from outside onto the Tones tab or a preset. A drag copies. Every row's right-click menu has the same order, with its keyboard shortcuts. By @crmne.
- **TonePush asks before replacing a preset.** Putting a tone in a slot that holds a preset says what goes and where it will still be; an empty slot is written at once. Several tones go in one step. By @crmne.
- **Every tone says which pedal it is for**: the HX model, or the firmware a StompStation PRO tone needs (1.5 or 2.x). A tone the connected pedal cannot play is marked, with the reason. By @crmne.
- **Publishing asks first, and your tones are listed.** The publish sheet shows the song, the tone, the pedal and who can see it: **Everyone** or **Only you**. A new version goes to the tone's existing song instead of a new one. **Mine** lists every tone and setlist you published, from any computer, and you can hide, rename or delete them there. Plays on TonePush are counted apart from downloads. By @crmne.
- **The StompStation PRO's 2.x chain is drawn and edited.** The board shows the chain as the pedal runs it: fourteen positions, fixed blocks locked, free positions as slots, and parallel blocks as lanes. Add a block from a free position, swap blocks by dragging, and join or split parallel paths. `tonepush pro set` sets the chain from the command line. Checked on a pedal at 2.0.10 by reading back each change. By @crmne.
- **The StompStation PRO saves on firmware 2.2.** TonePush now sends 2.2 smaller requests with short pauses, which keeps the pedal answering over USB even after your computer has used it as a sound card. Importing, renaming, moving, saving, clearing, IRs, NAM models, settings and restore were each checked on a pedal at 2.2.6 by reading back the result. A full backup of a 2.2 pedal takes about six minutes. By @crmne.
- **Patch releases of the StompStation PRO firmware count as the release they patch**, so a pedal on 1.5.10 or 2.0.8 saves like 1.5.12 or 2.0.10. On firmware TonePush does not know yet, a block's knobs can still be turned. By @crmne.
- **A Windows installer**, for x64 and ARM. It needs no administrator rights, adds TonePush to the Start menu, installs the `tonepush` command-line tool, and updates by running the next installer. The zip remains for running without installing. By @crmne.
- **Scrolling matches other apps:** a wheel notch moves further, and on Linux a touchpad glides on after you lift your fingers. By @crmne.

## Fixed

- **Windows finds a StompStation PRO.** Windows' own serial driver does not report the pedal's name, so 0.8.0 never found it there. TonePush now asks the port who it is. By @crmne.
- **The editor keeps moving while a StompStation PRO backs up**, its progress updates as it goes, and deleting many tones from the library at once no longer freezes the window. By @crmne.
- **A tone that cannot be played no longer leaves "Loading" on screen for good.** If the pedal goes, or you delete the tone while it waits, the audition ends and says why. By @crmne.
- **Paste and dropping files work together on Hyprland**, so dropping a WAV, a preset or the HX Edit installer on the window works on Wayland again. By @crmne.
- **The editor starts on old Windows graphics drivers**, and on Macs with a Touch Bar a closed window no longer lingers. By @crmne.
- **A button's shortcut sits on the same line as its label.** By @crmne.

## Known limitations

- NAM models cannot be reordered on firmware 2.0.x, because that firmware keeps playing the old model until it restarts.
- An HX Effects backup can still time out while reading the pedal's settings (#9), and an HX Stomp on firmware 3.80 that stays on "transferring data" (#5) is still being investigated.
- A copy unpacked from the Windows zip keeps updating as a zip. Install with the setup program once to switch.

## Thanks

Everyone who reported problems and tested on their own pedals.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/compare/v0.8.0...v0.9.0

name: TonePush 0.8.0
body:
TonePush 0.8.0 is a new editor. Your pedal's presets sit in a sidebar beside three pages, Edit, Library and Pedal; the chain is drawn like a pedalboard with your footswitches and expression pedals along the bottom; and there is a light theme. The StompStation PRO gets its firmware updates from TonePush and saves on firmware 2.0.10, and a long list of fixes makes backups, saving and switching presets safer on every pedal.

**Download TonePush:** [Mac](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.8.0/tonepush-v0.8.0-macos-universal.dmg) · [Windows](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.8.0/tonepush-v0.8.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip) · [Windows ARM](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.8.0/tonepush-v0.8.0-aarch64-pc-windows-msvc.zip) · [Linux](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.8.0/tonepush-v0.8.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz) · [Linux ARM](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.8.0/tonepush-v0.8.0-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz) · [Linux AppImage](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.8.0/tonepush-0.8.0-x86_64.AppImage)

![TonePush editing a preset on an HX Stomp: presets in the sidebar, a wah, a drive, the selected amp and two cabs in parallel along the chain, the amp's knobs, and the pedal's footswitches along the bottom](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.8.0/tonepush-v0.8.0-hx-edit.png)

![The same editor in the light theme, editing a StompStation PRO: its twelve blocks in a row with the amp selected and its NAM model and knobs below](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.8.0/tonepush-v0.8.0-pro-edit-light.png)

## New

- **A new editor.** The pedal's presets stay in a sidebar on every page, in the pedal's own banks. **Edit** shows the chain the way the pedal runs it, with lanes for parallel paths, the selected block's knobs, and your footswitches and expression pedals along the bottom. The model browser, footswitch assignments and snapshot table open in place of the knobs. **Library** is a table of your tones and setlists, compared with what is on the pedal. **Pedal** holds backups, impulse responses, NAM models and settings. The status bar and floating windows are gone. Text and numbers use Inter throughout. By @crmne.
- **A light theme.** TonePush follows your system's light or dark setting. By @crmne.
- **The connect page finds your pedal by itself.** Plug it in, or quit another editor that held it, and TonePush picks it up. The page also says whether this computer can reach USB pedals and whether HX Edit's model data is in place. By @crmne.
- **StompStation PRO firmware updates.** Start the pedal in update mode (once the Sonulab logo shows, hold UPD until the screen says Update Mode) and install Sonulab's `.zip` from the Pedal page, or with `tonepush pro firmware-update`. TonePush checks that the file is pedal firmware of the version you expect and that you have a fresh backup, confirms every batch it sends, and never restarts the pedal for you: it tells you when to. Tested with `tonepush pro firmware-update` by updating a pedal from 1.5.12 to 2.0.10, then 2.2.6, then back to 2.0.10, keeping every preset, IR and NAM model each time; the Pedal page runs the same steps. By @crmne.
- **StompStation PRO on firmware 2.0.10.** Saving, renaming, moving, clearing, importing presets, mono and stereo IRs and NAM models, global settings and restore were each checked on a pedal running 2.0.10 by reading the result back. NAM models cannot be reordered on 2.0.10, because that firmware keeps playing the old model until it restarts. By @crmne.
- **Firmware TonePush does not know yet opens read only, with presets live.** Browsing, export and backups work, and you can still pick presets and turn knobs; only writes to the pedal's memory wait. That covers 2.2.6 for now (see Known limitations). By @crmne.
- **The new filled app icon** stays recognisable at taskbar sizes. By @crmne.

## Fixed

- **A backup never deletes a folder.** Backing up an HX or a StompStation PRO into a folder that already held other files replaced it and deleted its contents. A backup now goes only into a new folder, an empty one, or an earlier backup. By @crmne.
- **A StompStation PRO backup is checked in full.** Only the start and end of each slot were compared, so a preset saved over itself under the same name went unnoticed: saving could unlock against an old backup, and a restore could skip that preset. Every preset and IR is now compared byte for byte, and each NAM model by its checksum. Automatic backups no longer replace the one taken earlier that day. By @crmne.
- **Helix backups cover every setlist**, not just the first, and `tonepush save` saves into the setlist that is loaded. By @crmne.
- **The editor follows presets and snapshots picked on the pedal.** Before, changing preset on the HX itself left the editor showing the old one, so Undo or Save could write it over the new one. By @crmne.
- **Switching presets asks before throwing away unsaved changes**, from every place that can switch: rows, arrow keys, menus, the preview's Load, a failed "Save, then load", and a cloud audition. By @crmne.
- **Saves and uploads are confirmed by what the pedal reads back.** A tempo or snapshot name that never landed counted as written, and an impulse response re-uploaded under the same name was taken as done before it was. By @crmne.
- **Dropping several WAV files gives each its own impulse-response slot**, instead of all of them overwriting one. By @crmne.
- **Moving a controller's travel no longer disconnects the pedal**, and tempos outside what the pedal accepts are refused with a message. By @crmne.
- **Pasting a block pastes the block you copied**, in this preset or another. By @crmne.
- **Closing the window waits for a transfer to finish**, instead of cutting it off and leaving the pedal on "transferring data". By @crmne.
- **`.hlx` import keeps the cab of an Amp+Cab**, and blocks keep the positions the file gives them. By @crmne.
- **Saved setlists are safer.** One unreadable file (such as a `._` file from macOS) no longer hides every setlist, and renaming an old setlist can no longer overwrite another one. By @crmne.
- **Cloud downloads are checked against the hash tonepush.rocks publishes**, so a Wi-Fi sign-in page can no longer land in your library, and a stalled download gives up instead of blocking the next one. By @crmne.
- **NAM model uploads to a StompStation PRO are confirmed correctly.** The pedal gzips a model again when it is read back, with its own header, so a correct upload was reported as failed; uploads are now checked by the model they contain. An upload under a name another slot already uses, which the pedal silently ignores, is refused with a message. By @crmne.
- **24-bit WAV impulse responses saved in the "extensible" format** (as ffmpeg and SoX write them) import. By @crmne.
- **Smaller fixes:** a preset address ending in an accented letter no longer crashes the CLI; snapshot names with control characters are refused instead of corrupting the preset; the CLI numbers blocks from 1 everywhere; knob columns sort negative values correctly; `install.sh` runs from any folder, quotes paths with spaces and leaves Homebrew's links alone on uninstall. By @crmne.

## Known limitations

- The StompStation PRO board shows the fixed twelve-block chain of firmware 1.5.12. On 2.x its parameters are all editable, but the new routing (parallel paths, free positions, the new effects as blocks) is not drawn yet.
- **Firmware 2.2.6 is read only.** Over USB it stops answering after a stretch of large replies, so a complete backup cannot be relied on, and saving waits for that. The cause looks like 2.2.6's new USB audio: once the computer has used the pedal as a sound card, the pedal's USB controller interrupts it constantly while TonePush reads. VoidX Control's slower, smaller requests seem to avoid it. If you need saving now, TonePush can put 2.0.10 back on the pedal (Pedal page, or `tonepush pro firmware-update`), keeping your presets, IRs and NAM models.
- An HX Effects backup can still time out while reading the pedal's settings (#9), and an HX Stomp on firmware 3.80 that stays on "transferring data" (#5) is still being investigated.
- 0.6.1 and earlier have no Update button, so moving to 0.8.0 from them is a manual download.

## Thanks

Everyone who reported problems and tested on their own pedals.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/compare/v0.7.0...v0.8.0

name: TonePush 0.7.0
body:
TonePush 0.7.0 updates itself: the Mac app and the Linux and Windows downloads fetch a new release, check its signature and install it when you restart. Parameters chosen from a menu can be changed, the HX Effects gets its own preset labels and can read its stored presets, and text is drawn the way the rest of your desktop draws it.

**Download TonePush:** [Mac](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.7.0/tonepush-v0.7.0-macos-universal.dmg) · [Windows](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.7.0/tonepush-v0.7.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip) · [Windows ARM](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.7.0/tonepush-v0.7.0-aarch64-pc-windows-msvc.zip) · [Linux](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.7.0/tonepush-v0.7.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz) · [Linux ARM](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.7.0/tonepush-v0.7.0-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz)

![TonePush showing TonePush 0.6.1 · 0.7.0 available in the status line, with an Update button beside it](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.7.0/tonepush-v0.7.0-update-button.png)

## New

- **Updates install from inside the editor.** When a newer release is out, an **Update** button appears beside the version in the status line. TonePush downloads the release, checks it against the signed checksums, and offers **Restart to update**. If the new version does not start, the previous one comes back. This works for the Mac app and the Linux and Windows downloads; Homebrew, AUR, `.deb` and `.rpm` installs keep updating through their package manager, and hovering the version says which one. TonePush now checks GitHub for a new release once a day instead of at every launch. By @crmne.
- **Release checksums are signed.** Every release's `checksums.txt` comes with a signature the updater verifies before installing anything. By @crmne.
- **Text looks like the rest of your desktop.** On Linux TonePush follows the desktop's font hinting setting, and in the dark theme text has the same weight as GTK apps beside it. Tone and setlist names in scripts Inter lacks, such as Chinese, Japanese, Arabic, Hebrew or Hindi, are drawn with your system's fonts instead of boxes. By @crmne.
- **HX Effects preset labels run 01A to 32D.** Presets, selection, renaming, saving and backups use the HX Effects' four presets to a bank, so `27A` in TonePush is `27A` on the pedal. The HX Stomp keeps its three. By @iibaranov-IG in #12; thanks @fruzz-urban for the report (#9).

## Fixed

- **Menu parameters can be changed.** Setting a parameter chosen from a menu, such as a compressor's Ratio or a phaser's Stages, was refused by the pedal with `error -3`, in both the editor and `tonepush set`. By @crmne; thanks @AC6y86 for the diagnosis and fix (#7).
- **An HX Effects can read and back up its stored presets.** Untouched factory presets, snapshots whose names were never typed, and controller assignments under a source the HX Stomp does not use no longer stop a backup at the first preset. By @crmne with @fruzz-urban's fix, tested on all 119 presets of their unit (#9).

## Known limitations

- 0.6.1 and earlier have no Update button, so moving to 0.7.0 is one last manual download.
- An HX Effects backup can still time out while reading the pedal's settings, after all presets are read (#9).
- Helix Floor, Rack and LT and the HX Stomp XL are still labelled with three presets to a bank.
- An HX Stomp on firmware 3.80 that stays on "transferring data" (#5) is still being investigated.

## Thanks

@AC6y86, @fruzz-urban and @iibaranov-IG, and everyone who reported problems and tested on their own pedals.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/compare/v0.6.1...v0.7.0

name: TonePush 0.6.1
body:
TonePush 0.6.1 keeps the editor responsive on Wayland when the compositor stops showing its window, draws frames in step with the display, and is the first release whose Mac app is signed and notarized by Apple, so it opens with a double-click and installs through Homebrew.

**Download TonePush:** [Mac](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.6.1/tonepush-v0.6.1-macos-universal.dmg) · [Windows](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.6.1/tonepush-v0.6.1-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip) · [Windows ARM](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.6.1/tonepush-v0.6.1-aarch64-pc-windows-msvc.zip) · [Linux](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.6.1/tonepush-v0.6.1-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz) · [Linux ARM](https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/releases/download/v0.6.1/tonepush-v0.6.1-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz)

## Fixed

- **The editor no longer freezes on Wayland when its window is out of sight.** Hyprland and other compositors stop drawing a window that is covered by a fullscreen or maximized one, sits on a hidden workspace, or is on a display that has gone to sleep. TonePush now stops painting while it is hidden instead of waiting for a frame that never comes, so the compositor no longer reports it as not responding. The connection to the pedal, changes to your tone library, and update checks keep being handled in the meantime. By @crmne; thanks @fgrehm, whose ZapFast report (crmne/zapfast#190) led to the fix now shared by TonePush, ZapFast, and Spotifast. (emilk/egui#8631, rust-windowing/winit#4709)
- **Frames follow the display's refresh on every platform.** 0.6.0 turned vsync off everywhere to avoid the freeze above, so every mouse movement drew a new frame as fast as the machine could. The editor now waits for the display again on macOS, Windows, X11, and Wayland. By @crmne.

## New

- **The Mac app is signed and notarized.** The DMG opens like any other Mac app, without the trip through **System Settings → Privacy & Security** that earlier versions needed, and the command-line tools in the Mac archive are notarized too. By @crmne.
- **Install with Homebrew:** `brew install --cask crmne/tap/tonepush` for the app, or `brew install crmne/tap/tonepush` for the `tonepush` and `tonepush-gui` binaries. By @crmne.
- **A ready-made Arch package:** `yay -S tonepush-bin` installs the released build with its udev rule and desktop entry. `tonepush` builds the release from source and `tonepush-git` the latest commit. By @crmne.

## Known limitations

- Downloads of 0.6.0 and earlier stay unnotarized; only this release and later open without the Privacy & Security step.
- These reports remain open and are not addressed here: an HX Stomp on firmware 3.80 that stays on "transferring data" (#5), `tonepush set` being unable to write enum parameters (#7), and parser and labelling problems on the HX Effects with firmware 3.80 (#9).

## Thanks

@fgrehm, and everyone who reported problems and tested on their own pedals.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/crmne/tonepush/compare/v0.6.0...v0.6.1

name: TonePush 0.2.1
body:
The release for people who browse. Riding the preset list quickly could wedge the pedal hard enough to need its power pulled; it cannot anymore.

## Fixed

- **Fast preset browsing no longer wedges the device.** A preset switch is a deferred operation, and the editor used to fire the next one while the last was still committing; the device jams after about a dozen stacked commits. A switch now completes fully before the next begins, and quick clicks through the list collapse to the preset you stop on, which also makes browsing feel instant. The hardware regression suite now includes the exact storm that caused a real wedge.

## Improved

- **Choice parameters are drop-down menus.** Mic selections and friends no longer pretend to be knobs.
- **Type any value.** Click a value, type it in the units shown, press Enter.
- **Double-click a knob** to return it to its factory default.
- **Parameter names** are now as large as their values.

## Install

See the [download page](https://docs.tonepush.rocks/download/) for every OS, Homebrew, and the AUR.

Line 6 and HX are trademarks of Yamaha Guitar Group; this project is not affiliated with them.

name: TonePush 0.2.0
body:
The release that welcomes you. On first launch, TonePush now walks you through the one-time setup itself.

## First launch, explained by the app

Without HX Edit's data files there are no model names, no knob ranges, and no artwork, so a welcome window now handles the whole thing:

- If **HX Edit is already installed** on the machine, TonePush copies its data automatically. No steps at all.
- Otherwise it points you at the HX Edit download, then takes the installer by **file picker**, a **Downloads folder check**, or **drag and drop**. Either installer works: the Mac `.dmg` or the Windows `.exe`, on any OS.
- The moment extraction finishes, names, knobs, and pictures appear in place. No restart.

The extractor now unwraps the whole Mac installer chain (dmg, pkg, gzip, cpio) with 7-Zip on Linux and Windows, and with hdiutil and pkgutil natively on macOS.

## Dependencies

- **Linux / Windows**: reading an HX Edit installer in-app needs 7-Zip (`p7zip` on most Linux distros; the AUR package suggests it). Not needed if HX Edit is installed on the same machine.
- **macOS**: nothing extra.

## Fixed

- Every file dialog on Linux (Browse, Export, Import) crashed the app due to an async runtime mismatch in the dialog library. All of them work now.

## Install

Grab your platform's build below, or see the [download page](https://docs.tonepush.rocks/download/) for per-OS instructions, Homebrew, and the AUR.

Line 6 and HX are trademarks of Yamaha Guitar Group; this project is not affiliated with them.

name: TonePush 0.1.0
body:
The first release of **TonePush**: an open-source editor for Line 6 HX-family devices. A cross-platform GUI, a scriptable CLI, and the reverse-engineered protocol documentation behind both. Built and verified operation by operation against an HX Stomp on firmware 3.80.

## Why it exists

HX Edit is macOS/Windows only, and its protocol was undocumented. TonePush runs on Linux too, edits the same scratch buffer HX Edit edits, and ships with [PROTOCOL.md](PROTOCOL.md): the whole wire protocol written up, so this editor is not the only thing that can ever be built on it.

## What it does

- **The signal chain, drawn as it is wired.** The main line never bends; a parallel branch hangs below it between a draggable fork and merge. Drag a block onto the offered branch to run it in parallel, drag the fork and merge to move where the path divides, and choose how the split divides: Y, A/B, crossover, or dynamic.
- **Editing.** Swap models from a searchable thumbnail browser with HX Edit's own artwork, turn knobs with values formatted exactly as HX Edit formats them, drag to reorder, undo/redo with the keyboard.
- **Presets travel byte for byte.** Copy, paste, import, export, and setlist backup carry the device's own document verbatim, so nothing is lost in translation.
- **Snapshots, setlists, tempo, IRs, device settings.** The rest of what HX Edit does on an HX Stomp, each verified against the hardware.

## Install

**Linux / macOS**: download the archive for your platform below, unpack, and run the binaries. Or clone and run `./install.sh`, which also sets up the udev rule (Linux), desktop entry, and app bundle (macOS).

**Windows**: unpack the zip and run `stompchain-gui.exe`.

Model names, ranges, and artwork come from HX Edit's own data files: run `tools/hxresources/extract.sh /path/to/HX_Edit.dmg` (or `.exe`) with an installer downloaded from [line6.com](https://line6.com/software/). Without it everything still works, just with numbers where names would be.

Quit HX Edit before connecting. It holds the device exclusively.

## Honest limits

This is a 0.1: it works, and it wants testing. The tested device is an HX Stomp on firmware 3.80. Helix and LT parse and render (two DSP paths, four lanes) but have not met real hardware yet. If something misbehaves, an issue with the `stompchain chain` output and what you expected is gold.

Nothing here is derived from Line 6 source code; the protocol was reconstructed by observing USB traffic. Line 6 and HX are trademarks of Yamaha Guitar Group; this project is not affiliated with them.
